title: MAML-residual transformer for few-shot prediction of targeted therapy response in NSCLC.
summary: The MAML-RT radiomics model predicted targeted-therapy response in NSCLC with accuracy 0.91 and AUC 0.93 in 300 patients; under a 50-case few-shot setting, AUC was 0.76. In an independent external validation cohort, AUC was 0.85 and accuracy 0.88. These are retrospective model evaluations, not evidence of improved treatment outcomes.
ai_technology: The MAML-RT framework combines model-agnostic meta-learning and residual transformers to predict targeted-therapy response from NSCLC radiomics in few-shot cohorts.
organization: Affiliated Dongyang Hospital; Wenzhou Medical University

evidence.tested: MAML-RT combines model-agnostic meta-learning and residual transformers to predict targeted-therapy response from radiomics in NSCLC. It achieved AUC 0.93 in a 300-patient cohort, AUC 0.76 with 50 cases, and AUC 0.85 in an independent external cohort.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and prospective real-world benefit are not established in the reviewed study.
evidence.ai_role: The MAML-RT framework combines model-agnostic meta-learning and residual transformers to predict targeted-therapy response from NSCLC radiomics in few-shot cohorts.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
